queue.title: Change: 'a dead thing holds nothing' (F53b + F65 + F60 guard)
queue.detail: Run openspec-propose for a change named `a-dead-thing-holds-nothing`. Decisions are made and written in openspec/explorations/2026-08-26-what-is-still-unanswered.md sections 3, 4 and 6 - use them as design input. Three behaviours, one principle: an ended thing stops exerting force. (1) F53(b): NEVER null task.loop_id - the operator's instruction is 'keep the history to retrace it later', so the column is history and stays on every task in every state. Instead change the GATE: `_adopt_document_tasks` (api/v1/jobs.py:185) restricts to `loop_id IS NULL`; make that 'owned by a LIVE loop', the same archived_at.is_(None) shape already shipped for _check_spec_document_conflict in migration 0090. The scheduler re-queues a review when evidence appears, so nothing is lost, and the roster stops being held hostage (it currently 409s POST /agents/{name}/archive). queue.title: Change: a separate review capacity (the reviewer ladder)
queue.detail: Run openspec-propose for the reviewer-ladder change. Decision recorded in openspec/explorations/2026-08-26-what-is-still-unanswered.md section 2: option 2, a SEPARATE review capacity. Today `_agents_that_are_free` (hub/hub/scheduler.py:916) answers one question - 'is this agent free' - and rung 2 uses it for two different ones. Split them: 'free to be given work' keeps the current rule; 'free to review' gets its own. Measured justification: LIVE_STATUSES includes under_review, and staffing a review makes the reviewer the assignee, so a review consumes an agent entirely; ledger-stress has 0 of 3 agents free and review_unstaffed has fired 10 times. Rejected alternative to record: merely excluding under_review from what makes an agent unfree - it fixes the measured case but leaves one question doing two jobs. Note D4's pile-up argument is about BEING GIVEN WORK, and a review is a bounded turn against somebody else's commit, not an accumulation of ownership.

NEW, measured and FIXED during this prep: e2e.py's `clean` used shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True), which on Windows is a lie - git marks everything under .git/objects read-only, rmtree raises on the first one, the error is swallowed, and `clean` prints 'removed' over a directory that is still there. Now goes through _rmtree_windows, which clears the read-only bit and REPORTS if the tree survives anyway. Verified causally on the leftover directory the old code had abandoned.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F52 correction): isolated reproduction of a Claude Code CLI permission refusal is NOT reliable from inside this session's own Bash tool, even with CLAUDE_CODE_*/CLAUDECODE env vars and this machine's ~/.claude/settings.json (defaultMode: auto) both stripped, and even spawning through a real winpty.PtyProcess pseudo-terminal matching PtySession exactly. Six different repro configurations all succeeded where two real production runs failed on the identical command text. Whatever triggers the refusal is specific to the full production turn (large injected system-prompt-file context, or something else not yet isolated) - do not treat a clean isolated repro as proof a CLI-level refusal finding is wrong; it proved the opposite of what it looked like it would here.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F52 correction): `record_evidence`'s `locator` argument is free text - "a path, a command, a run id" per its own docstring, never a commit sha the agent must produce. An agent that reads a task's 'commit your work and record evidence naming the commit' framing as 'evidence requires a successful commit first' is over-interpreting; the two are independent and evidence can be recorded before, or even without, any commit.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (Q4 retry): an agent registered via POST /agents/register (contact_mode: poll, self_registered: true - what e2e.py cmd_agent always does) cannot be a loop/job spawn target: POST /jobs/{id}/run 409s with '... is a self-registered poll agent and manages its own execution'. Only a Hub-managed agent (POST /agents, self_registered: false) can run a flow job. e2e.py-registered agents are fine for e2e.py turn (direct interview-style triggers) but not for anything that goes through the scheduler.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (Q4 close, iteration 7): a Loop's `stop_when_queue_empties` is evaluated on the NEXT scheduler tick, not synchronously the instant the last task in its queue reaches a terminal status - a job whose cron will never fire again (this iteration deliberately used one) can sit with an empty, fully-completed queue and `enabled: true` indefinitely, with nothing self-correcting it. Very likely harmless for a real cron (it would tick and self-stop normally) but means a loop must never be assumed to have disabled itself just because its queue looks empty - always disable explicitly, per the standing rule, rather than trusting the stop condition to have already fired.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F53/F54): _check_spec_document_conflict (hub/hub/api/v1/jobs.py) never excludes archived loops, so a document claimed by a loop that is later archived - even one that never fired a single turn - can never be claimed by a new loop again, and _adopt_document_tasks has no path to release the loop_id it already stamped onto that document's tasks. Fixed as part of F54: create_job now checks this conflict BEFORE committing the job row (it used to commit first, so a 409 left an enabled job behind - that half is fixed and live-verified). The archived-loop-permanently-claims-the-document half is still open as F53, unfixed, for Q6.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F55): on this machine, datetime.now(timezone.utc) returns the IDENTICAL value across five consecutive calls with no delay - Windows clock resolution is coarser than the microsecond precision the value implies. Any ORDER BY created_at DESC with a non-monotonic secondary sort (id.desc(), where id is a random short_id()) can silently pick the wrong 'latest' row on a timestamp tie. latest_checkpoint_for_loop (hub/hub/checkpoints.py) has exactly this shape and is now F55, unfixed - test_flow_checkpoint_lineage.py flakes on it (confirmed pre-existing, not caused by any change this session): 2 of 6 bare re-runs failed on the unmodified branch tip. If this file is ever red, re-run it once before treating it as a new regression, and do not 'fix' it by loosening the assertion - the ordering bug is real.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F56, iteration 8): InboundQueueEntry.state only becomes 'delivered' atomically WITH a Run's creation (inbound_queue.py's deliver helper). A TriggerAgentError raised inside trigger_agent_directly BEFORE that point (an unresolvable review_task_id, an archived agent, any other pre-flight refusal) leaves the entry state='queued' forever with delivery_attempts stuck at 0, because return_run_entries (the thing that counts attempts and abandons at DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_LIMIT) only runs for a Run that was created and then failed post-spawn. schedule_agent always retries the SAME oldest queued entry first regardless of what a new trigger asked for, so one such poisoned entry wedges an agent's entire queue indefinitely with a misleading 'queued' response naming an unrelated task. Fixed in hub/hub/turn_scheduler.py this iteration - if a future session sees an agent stuck on a nonsensical waiting_reason, check inbound_queue_entries for an old queued entry sitting ahead of everything else before assuming anything else is wrong.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (iteration 10): scripts/drive/aw.py's api() ALREADY prepends /api/v1 - passing a path that also starts with /api/v1 double-prefixes and 404s silently (looks like 'project not found' or 'not found', not an obviously-wrong-URL error). Pass paths like /projects/{id}/tasks, not /api/v1/projects/{id}/tasks. Also: the evidence routes are doubly-nested by the router composition - full path is /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/project/spec/evidence (not /projects/{id}/evidence, not /projects/{id}/spec/evidence) - spec.py's router has prefix="/project" (singular) and is itself mounted under project_resources_router's /projects/{project_id}. e2e.py's project argument to `turn`/`task-set`/etc. must be the project ID (proj-xxxx), not the human slug used by `state` in some contexts - ledger-stress as a literal string 404s on POST endpoints.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (iteration 8): after unblocking a wedged agent, expect a self-drain - the completion path reschedules the same agent, so backlogged entries can fire several more real runs with no further triggering. Check `runs`/`task_transitions` afterward rather than assuming only the run you explicitly watched happened; this iteration found a third task moved to revision_needed this way that nobody had gone looking for.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (iteration 17): a fresh `sqlite3.connect('file:...?mode=ro', uri=True)` read against the beta trial database can return STALE data - a row that is already committed 'failed' (with `ended_at` set) can still read back as `status='running'`/`ended_at=None` moments later on a brand-new read-only connection, because the db is in WAL mode and `mode=ro` connections are not guaranteed to see recent WAL-resident commits. `e2e.py`'s own `state`/`ro()` helper uses the identical pattern and is equally exposed. This produced a near-miss: a run that had actually failed via its normal 600s timeout looked, on first read, like it was stuck 'running' 70 minutes past its own deadline with the timeout mechanism silently not firing - a plausible severe finding that a second read (same query, moments later) flatly contradicted. Any time-sensitive 'is this stuck/still running' claim from this database needs at least two reads before being trusted or written up.

`$TMPDIR` is UNSET in this Bash environment. `some-cmd > "$TMPDIR/x.log"` resolves to `/x.log` and fails with 'Permission denied' - and if it is part of a compound command the overall exit code comes from the LAST command, so it looks like it succeeded. Cost one wasted background watch this session. Use an absolute path under the scratchpad directory.

CI triggers ONLY on push to master and PRs targeting master (.github/workflows/ci.yml). A feature branch gets NO CI at all, however many times you push it. Do not expect CI feedback on this run's branch; the local suites are the only signal until the operator merges.

Only Python 3.11 exists on this machine (`py -0p` lists one entry). The codebase targets 3.12, so 3.12 CANNOT be tested locally - only CI covers it, and only on master. Do not claim a change is 3.12-clean from a local run.

The events table is `event_logs` (plural) and its column is `event_type`, NOT `event_log` / `kind`. Both wrong guesses cost a query each this session. Columns: id, project_id, event_type, agent, loop_id, data, severity, timestamp.

Jobs CANNOT be deleted. `DELETE /projects/{p}/jobs/{j}` returns 400 with 'jobs are archived, not deleted - archive this job instead; nothing was removed' (design D16, deliberate). Use `POST /projects/{p}/jobs/{j}/archive`.

`/api/v1/projects` and the other operator routes want `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Sending `X-API-Key: <key>` returns 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' - and if you pipe that through a JSON parser expecting a list you get an empty result that looks like 'no projects exist' rather than an auth failure. Check the status code before believing an empty list.

Writing document content through a bash heredoc keeps failing - this session it died with 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching' on prose containing backticks and quotes. Use the Write tool for document bodies, and a small Python script read from a file for any bulk edit.
method_reminders: Use the real surface. Never simulate a step. If something has no API, that absence IS the finding - write it down and continue. This is how 'no integration step exists' surfaced.
Play the operator honestly, and leave something unanswered. A tester who answers everything never discovers which questions silently evaporate.

Watch the seams: between exploring and proposing, between an approved document and a task, between a completed task and a reviewed one, between one agent and the next. The defects are there, not inside a phase.
Read what the agent actually said. The transcript is evidence. Do not dismiss an agent's account of its own failure - verify it.
Follow peer-triggered work, not just what you triggered. Runs an agent starts by messaging another take a different path through the code, and that is where posture and continuity get lost.

Never accept 'the tests pass' as evidence. Run them yourself, then recompute a result by hand and compare. Check the rows, not the chat: an agent's summary of what it did is a claim, the rows are the fact.
A green suite agrees with broken behaviour more often than you expect. Mutation-check anything you claim: delete the line the test exists for, and watch a NAMED test fail.
The best evidence is the failure you did not stage. Watch for unprovoked failures and write them up when they happen.
Say when you contaminated your own test. Testing code you wrote yourself inherits your blind spots - a finding you did NOT make is weaker evidence, and the operator needs to know which is which.
Record what HELD, not only what broke. A gate that correctly refused something is a result the next session needs.
